summary.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 16% YoY to ₹529 crores and adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to ₹89 crores, with margin at 16.8%. Adjusted PAT was ₹32 crores versus ₹26 crores a year earlier. Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. Management said the ₹150 crore capex (sheet metal capacity now 108,000 tons) has just commenced, while the ₹290 crore Hyderabad greenfield casting project is about ₹60 crores spent. Margins were flat YoY, which management attributed to pre-operating manpower and variable costs ahead of operating leverage.

segments.name: Traction Motor and Railway Components
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 28% of Q1 revenue; management flagged some softness in traction motors this quarter.

segments.name: Power Generation
segments.commentary: 15% of revenue. Data Centers (power generation side) at 5% of revenue, with direct US exports for one customer and domestic supply plus re-export for others.

segments.name: Industrial and Commercial / Mining, Oil & Gas / Special Application Motors
segments.commentary: Industrial and commercial 12%, Mining, Oil & Gas 10% (up from ~5% of revenue per management), Special Application Motors 9%. Renewable energy 3%, other 17%.

segments.name: Machine Components vs Casting
segments.commentary: Machined components growing faster than raw castings; machining utilisation 86% (vs 82%) is the main bottleneck, not order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Lamination volume target raised to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons.
FY27 EBITDA guided at roughly ₹370 crores based on current outlook.
Management expects overall margins to improve as sheet metal utilisation moves toward 80%; did not quantify quarterly path.
Next year (FY28) at 90,000 tons operating level: turnover above ₹2,500 crores and EBITDA margin of about 17%-17.2% (ex incremental Lamination capex).
Casting capacity at 24,000 tons; casting volume guidance upgraded to about 17,000 tons (from ~16,000 previously referenced).
Export direct volumes expected to improve QoQ in Q2-Q4 as new capacity ramps.
Longer-term margin aspiration upwards of 18%, closer to 18%-18.5% in about three years, per management.
Effective tax rate for full FY27 expected around 25%.

Other income (state capex incentive) not expected this year; management leaning toward claiming from next year, dependent on government approval of 9-year period; ~₹70 crores of incentive receivable expected in 9-12 months.
capex_capacity: ₹150 crore capex recently commenced: sheet metal capacity raised to 108,000 tons, with casting and machining augmented.
₹290 crore greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad: ~₹60 crores spent so far (land acquisition started); ~30% infrastructure and ~70% plant and equipment; commissioning targeted by Q1 FY30.
Machining capacity to reach 1,080,000 machine hours from the ₹290 crore capex, added progressively each quarter; casting capacity now 24,000 tons.
Sheet metal headroom only ~8,000 tons at 80% operating efficiency; FY28 capacity capex expected around Q3-Q4 FY27 timeframe.
Potential Bangalore fully owned facility in FY28-FY29 (not board-approved): ~₹200 crores building plus ~₹200 crores equipment.
Sheet metal utilisation 73% (vs 70%), machining 86% (vs 82%), casting and fabrication 72%.
demand_pricing: China Plus One, Europe-to-India manufacturing shift and electrification cited as demand drivers; indirect exports via Indian operations of global customers growing.
Data Centers, railways, metros, mining and off-highway named as strong visibility areas; management cautious on AI data-center durability.
Mining order inquiries from US and Europe described as very good; Mining grew from ~5% to ~10% of revenue.

Growth in high value-added Lamination assemblies (rotor shaft, stator) driven by Data Centers, special industrial, mining, off-highway and wind; volume up ~37% per analyst calculation vs 16% for Lamination.
Direct exports flat (₹137 crores last year vs ₹139 crores this year per analyst), while domestic sales grew 23%.
Incremental LPG costs being passed through to customers per management.
